items.basis: The claimed mechanism of energy dissipation through elastomer shear deformation and sliding components directly contradicts the fundamental behavior of elastomeric bearings, where energy dissipation primarily occurs through viscoelastic hysteresis of the elastomer material itself, not through sliding interfaces which would introduce unpredictable stick-slip behavior and compromise the bearing's ability to provide consistent vertical support

The boundary condition allowing shear deformations up to 300-400% of elastomeric thickness is impossible to maintain with sliding components, as such extreme deformations would cause the sliding interfaces to separate completely, violating the laminated bearing's structural integrity and load transfer capability

The provided evidence includes a study on organic electrochemical transistors in bioelectronics (doi:10.1002/advs.202513422) which is completely irrelevant to elastomeric bridge bearings, demonstrating a fundamental lack of domain-specific knowledge in the candidate's evidence base

The candidate fails to demonstrate any superiority over the baseline by not addressing the primary failure modes of creep and ozone cracking, instead introducing new potential failure modes at sliding interfaces that are not adequately quantified or compared to baseline performance

The novel design variable of sliding interface material and surface roughness cannot be manufactured with the precision required for bridge bearings, where even micron-level variations would create stress concentrations leading to premature failure under cyclic loading

The testable prediction of "less than 10% vertical deflection drift after 75 years of simulated traffic cycling" is meaningless without specifying the exact loading conditions, environmental exposure parameters, and baseline performance metrics against which the comparison is made
